findings.title: Delete routing contradicts the collision-case remediation path
findings.description: The Data Flow states "**Delete:** mirrors write — deletes from whichever project file the key's scope maps to. `migrate-personal` … is the one exception that touches the *other* project file, by design." Under that rule, `cf config unset git.integration_branch --project` (a personal-scope key) deletes from `.context-forge.local.toml` only — i.e., it would remove the developer's *live* personal value and leave the stale `.context-forge.toml` copy in place. But the Migration Plan's Collision Semantics (line 146) names "`cf config unset <key> --project`" as the explicit way to clear the stale *shared-file* copy, and Verification Walkthrough step 9 (line 259) runs exactly that command and expects `.context-forge.toml` to be clean afterward. As written, those two passages cannot both hold: the walkthrough step fails (finding persists) and, worse, the user's personal value is destroyed — the exact hazard the collision section was written to prevent. The requirement left unmet is the plan entry's "defined migration/compat story": the story's remediation path for a personal key present in *both* files needs a specified delete semantic (e.g., delete of a personal-scope key also clears its shared-file copy, with an explicit call-out that this is a deliberate, second exception to the routing rule — or a different remediation mechanism such as a flag or the checker rule). One sentence of clarification resolves it.

findings.title: MCP `config_get` tool description becomes stale and is outside the stated configTools update scope
findings.description: The Technical Scope limits the `configTools.ts` change to "surface both project config paths," and the Development Approach step 7 repeats only the `configPaths` response addition. The existing `config_get` tool description in `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/configTools.ts` ("Resolution order: project config → user config → built-in default") becomes factually wrong for personal keys once the precedence is project-personal → project-shared → user → default. Since agent-facing tool descriptions are the guidance surface for this tool, the one-line description update should be included in the configTools change (and a matching note for `cf config get`'s help text if it states resolution order).

findings.title: Migration/compat story and failure modes meet the plan's requirement
findings.description: The plan entry's "defined migration/compat story for projects that already committed personal keys" is covered end-to-end: read-time fallback (no functional regression, verified consistent with the current `get()` precedence in `ConfigManager.ts`), a `warning`-severity `ConsistencyChecker` rule that surfaces through both `cf check` and MCP `workflow_check` (both confirmed to run the full `checkAll` suite), a dedicated `migrate-personal` command with explicit collision semantics, and per-path failure handling (write-personal-then-delete-shared ordering, per-key failure continuation, idempotent re-run, `cf init` gitignore append aborting via the existing `handleError` path — verified present in `init.ts`). The rejection of `fixAction` wiring is justified against the actual closed union type in `introspection/types.ts`.

findings.title: Boundaries, dependency directions, and proportionality are correct
findings.description: Routing is kept inside `ConfigManager` (core) with unchanged `get/set/delete/list` signatures, so all verified call sites (CLI `config.ts`/`guides.ts`/`check.ts`/`next.ts`/`status.ts`, `branchGuard.ts` via 916, MCP `configTools.ts`) need no changes — dependency direction (callers → ConfigManager) is preserved. The `916` reference is correctly historical (916's prerequisite fix is merged; `--project [id]`/`--global` verified in `config.ts`), and the design's `dependencies: [914]` matches the body and the plan. Nothing is overweight relative to the plan entry: no dry-run/confirmation machinery (explicitly deferred in Special Considerations), no gitignore template (deferred to the plan's Future Work), no CLI surface change — and the explicitly-excluded list correctly fences off user-scope behavior and auto-fix wiring.

structured_findings.summary: Delete routing contradicts the collision-case remediation path
MCP `config_get` tool description becomes stale and is outside the stated configTools update scope
Migration/compat story and failure modes meet the plan's requirement
Boundaries, dependency directions, and proportionality are correct
